subject: SET statement
notes: kb/Work PB450 half 2 - the LAST printed general format of 14.9.39.2 whose grammar shape was not the figure's. The printed Format 7 was RE-RENDERED here (specs-private PDF p760 / folio 730 at 300 dpi) rather than taken from the transcription: `SET { ADDRESS OF data-name-1 | identifier-5 } ... TO identifier-6`, the brace a PLAIN required choice, the `...` OUTSIDE it, ADDRESS and TO underlined and OF NOT - and the figure note says the same in words, "The braces are a plain required choice - exactly one of the two alternatives - and the following `...` repeats the braced receiving operand" (cite.py --check 14.9.39.2 OK). The grammar held TWO fixed productions split on the SENDER's spelling, each hard-coding arity one, so four cells of the printed cross-product were a bare COBOL0001 at every edition. MEASURED on this worktree's own build BEFORE the fix: `SET ADDRESS OF B1 ADDRESS OF B2 TO P1` -> `COBOL0001: unexpected 'ADDRESS'`; `SET P1 P2 TO ADDRESS OF REC1` -> `cannot parse construct near 'REC1'`; `SET ADDRESS OF B1 P1 TO P2` -> `unexpected 'P1'`; `SET ADDRESS OF B1 TO ADDRESS OF R1` -> `unexpected 'ADDRESS'`. AFTER: all four compile and answer the values 14.9.39.4 GR12/GR13 and 8.4.3.11.4 GR1 compute (B1A=[AAAA] B2A=[AAAA] / B1A=[BBBB] / B1A=[CCCC] / B1A=[DDDD]). The rule is ONE production whose repeated unit is a NAMED rule, and since kb/Work PB4231 it is the one rule for every SET ... TO shape, `setToStatement : SET setToReceiver+ TO setToSender`; the receiver carries its own kind (`ADDRESS()` present = data-name-1, absent = identifier-5) instead of a binder re-deriving it from token positions - the discipline half 1 landed for Formats 3 and 4, held for this one by the same drift test. A statement that spells the ADDRESS phrase (an ADDRESS OF data-name-1 receiver or a data-address-identifier sender) is Format 7 by that spelling (SetToStatementCst.SpellsAddressPhrase routes it to PtrBinder.BindSetAddress); for every other `SET X TO NULL` Format 7's identifier-6 may be the predefined address NULL (SR19) and Format 5's sender the predefined object reference NULL, so only the receiver's category tells them apart, which is a BIND question. setToSender offers NULL first, so SLL predicts the statement (kb/Work PB4231: 75 legal corpus programs used to bail the SLL pass on it), pinned by unit:PrintedFormatAlternativeDriftTests.SetToSender_OffersNullFirst_AndSetStatementOffersOneToRule and unit:SetToStatementSllDriftTests. The other sixteen formats' shapes were swept and none carries a hard-coded arity: Formats 8, 9, 15 and the ENTRY extension already write `dataReference+`, Format 16's printed receiving operand IS one operand, and Format 6 is refused by name (COBOL1707). Re-affirmed 2026-10-22 (kb/Work PB3530) against the figure regenerated from the printed page: render_figure.py's brace-group layout now keeps every alternative inside its own enclosure, so the diagram's layout changed while its words did not (sweep_figures.py's word gate); the verdict stands on the printed format. retired-witness: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4#setAddressStatement (kb/Work PB4231 deleted the rule: every SET ... TO shape is the one setToStatement rule, which carries Format 7's receiving brace as setToReceiver and its senders as setToSender)
